metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results (Volume IV) Factsheets – Canadian provinces

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 financial literacy results for eight Canadian provinces using the OECD PISA 2022 database. The document does not specify the exact sampling-weight variable names or whether replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) were used; therefore, the weighting approach cannot be confirmed from the provided text. The factsheet cautions that one or more PISA sampling standards were not reached for Canada overall, which implies that standard PISA sampling/precision requirements may affect interpretability of estimates. For analysts using the underlying PISA 2022 microdata, the appropriate approach is to apply the official PISA sampling weights and replicate weights as defined in the PISA 2022 Reader’s Guide/technical documentation, and to use the provided plausible-value/scaling procedures for the financial literacy scale.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a descriptive OECD factsheet summarizing PISA 2022 financial literacy results (means, proficiency-level distributions, and associations) rather than reporting an original student-level predictive model with an explicit plausible-value (PV) and missing-data handling pipeline. PVs are part of PISA’s scaling framework for cognitive achievement, but the factsheet does not describe how PVs were combined or how missing responses were handled in the analysis. As a result, the PV and missing-data handling details are not reported in the provided text, and extracting them would require the PISA 2022 Volume IV technical documentation/Reader’s Guide.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the PISA 2022 financial literacy assessment sample for the eight participating Canadian provinces (Alberta, British Columbia, Manitoba, New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador, Nova Scotia, Ontario, and Prince Edward Island). The factsheet does not report additional exclusions (e.g., complete-case rules) or further task/module restrictions beyond participation in the financial literacy assessment.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD factsheet summarizes PISA 2022 financial literacy results for eight Canadian provinces. Financial literacy was assessed via a computer-based test administered to sampled students, with students split into two groups: one group received financial literacy plus either mathematics or reading, while the other received the core PISA subjects; both groups were assessed for a total of 120 minutes. The factsheet reports that students in the Canadian provinces scored an average of 519 points (above the OECD average of 498), with 13% below Level 2 and 15% at Level 5. It also describes how financial literacy relates to mathematics and reading performance (about 77% of variation explained by those domains) and provides descriptive associations with student characteristics, saving and spending behaviours, and exposure to financial education at school. Interpretation is cautioned because PISA sampling standards were not reached for Canada overall, and the document does not provide the underlying technical details on PV combination or missing-data handling.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet (descriptive reporting) rather than an empirical machine-learning or predictive modeling study. Consequently, there is no ML algorithm evaluation, no explicit PV-combination or missing-data handling method described in the provided text, and no target-variable-specific predictive performance metrics to tabulate. The extraction therefore leaves main_findings and confounders_identified empty by design, while still capturing the assessment scope, sample size, and reported proficiency/association results.
